requirements.quote:
In TLS 1.3, as opposed to previous versions of TLS, all
   ciphers are modeled as "Authenticated Encryption with Associated
   Data" (AEAD) [RFC5116].
requirements.required_behavior: use an AEAD cipher construction
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using a separate non-AEAD encryption and MAC construction
requirements.why_checkable: Negotiated cipher suites and record-protection calls identify the cryptographic construction.

requirements.quote:
Each encrypted record consists of a
   plaintext header followed by an encrypted body
requirements.required_behavior: emit the record header in plaintext followed by the encrypted body
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encrypting the outer header or placing the body before it
requirements.why_checkable: The outer wire framing and encryption boundary are explicit.

requirements.quote:
an encrypted body, which itself contains
   a type and optional padding.
requirements.condition: constructing the encrypted body of a TLS 1.3 record
requirements.required_behavior: include the inner content type and place any optional padding inside the encrypted body
requirements.forbidden_behavior: exposing the actual content type or padding outside encryption
requirements.why_checkable: Decrypted inner plaintext and outer wire bytes reveal the placement.

requirements.quote: opaque content[TLSPlaintext.length];
requirements.required_behavior: encode content as exactly TLSPlaintext.length opaque bytes in the first field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using a different content length or field order
requirements.why_checkable: The dependent field length and first position are explicit.

requirements.quote: ContentType type;
requirements.required_behavior: encode a ContentType field immediately after content
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omitting or reordering the inner type field
requirements.why_checkable: The field type and ordered position are explicit.

requirements.quote: uint8 zeros[length_of_padding];
requirements.required_behavior: encode the padding as octets after the type field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: placing padding before the type field
requirements.why_checkable: The padding element width and final position are explicit.

requirements.quote: ContentType opaque_type = application_data; /* 23 */
requirements.required_behavior: set opaque_type to application_data value 23 as the first field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using another outer content type or field order
requirements.why_checkable: The first header octet has a fixed value.

requirements.quote: ProtocolVersion legacy_record_version = 0x0303; /* TLS v1.2 */
requirements.required_behavior: set legacy_record_version to 0x0303 after opaque_type
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using another value or field position
requirements.why_checkable: The two-byte header field and its position are fixed.

requirements.quote: uint16 length;
requirements.required_behavior: encode length as uint16 after legacy_record_version
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omitting, reordering, or using another width
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and ordered position are explicit.

requirements.quote: opaque encrypted_record[TLSCiphertext.length];
requirements.required_behavior: encode encrypted_record as exactly TLSCiphertext.length opaque bytes after length
requirements.forbidden_behavior: a ciphertext body whose byte count differs from length or is out of order
requirements.why_checkable: The dependent vector length and final position are explicit.

requirements.quote: content:  The TLSPlaintext.fragment value
requirements.required_behavior: copy TLSPlaintext.fragment into content without semantic alteration
requirements.forbidden_behavior: substituting different content bytes
requirements.why_checkable: The pre-protection and inner content byte strings can be compared.

requirements.quote:
type:  The TLSPlaintext.type value containing the content type of the
      record.
requirements.required_behavior: copy TLSPlaintext.type into the inner type field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encoding a different actual content type
requirements.why_checkable: The outer plaintext type and inner type values can be compared.

requirements.quote:
zeros:  An arbitrary-length run of zero-valued bytes may appear in
      the cleartext after the type field.
requirements.required_behavior: encode every padding byte as zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using a nonzero padding byte
requirements.why_checkable: Padding bytes are directly visible after AEAD decryption.

requirements.quote:
zeros:  An arbitrary-length run of zero-valued bytes may appear in
      the cleartext after the type field.
requirements.required_behavior: place the padding after the inner type field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: placing padding before or within content or before type
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized inner-plaintext field order is deterministic.

requirements.quote:
senders to pad any TLS record by a chosen amount as long as
      the total stays within record size limits.
requirements.required_behavior: keep the resulting record within the applicable record-size limits
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using padding that makes the record exceed its size limit
requirements.why_checkable: The total encoded size can be checked after padding is selected.

requirements.quote:
opaque_type:  The outer opaque_type field of a TLSCiphertext record
      is always set to the value 23 (application_data)
requirements.required_behavior: set outer opaque_type to 23
requirements.forbidden_behavior: exposing the actual inner content type in opaque_type
requirements.why_checkable: The first byte of every TLSCiphertext header is inspectable.

requirements.quote:
The actual content type of the record is found
      in TLSInnerPlaintext.type after decryption.
requirements.condition: dispatching a successfully decrypted TLSCiphertext record
requirements.required_behavior: obtain the actual content type from TLSInnerPlaintext.type
requirements.forbidden_behavior: dispatching protected content according to outer opaque_type
requirements.why_checkable: Post-decryption dispatch can be traced to the inner type byte.

requirements.quote:
legacy_record_version:  The legacy_record_version field is always
      0x0303.
requirements.required_behavior: set legacy_record_version to 0x0303
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using another legacy record version
requirements.why_checkable: The record header contains a fixed two-byte value.

requirements.quote:
length:  The length (in bytes) of the following
      TLSCiphertext.encrypted_record
requirements.required_behavior: make length equal the byte count of the following encrypted_record
requirements.forbidden_behavior: a declared length inconsistent with the ciphertext body
requirements.why_checkable: The header value can be compared with the available body bytes.

requirements.quote:
which is the sum of the lengths of
      the content and the padding, plus one for the inner content type,
      plus any expansion added by the AEAD algorithm.
requirements.required_behavior: compute content length plus padding length plus one content-type octet plus AEAD expansion
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omitting or double-counting any component
requirements.why_checkable: Every term in the length equation is measurable.

requirements.quote:
The length
      MUST NOT exceed 2^14 + 256 bytes.
requirements.required_behavior: limit TLSCiphertext.length to at most 16640 bytes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: a TLSCiphertext.length greater than 16640
requirements.why_checkable: The ciphertext length field has an exact upper bound.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that receives a
      record that exceeds this length MUST terminate the connection with
      a "record_overflow" alert.
requirements.condition: an endpoint receives TLSCiphertext.length greater than 16640
requirements.required_behavior: terminate the connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accepting, truncating, or continuing after the oversized record
requirements.why_checkable: An oversized ciphertext record has a fixed terminal alert.

requirements.quote:
encrypted_record:  The AEAD-encrypted form of the serialized
      TLSInnerPlaintext structure.
requirements.required_behavior: AEAD-encrypt the serialized TLSInnerPlaintext structure
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encrypting a different serialization or leaving it unprotected
requirements.why_checkable: Known keys and inner bytes can reproduce the ciphertext input and output.

requirements.quote:
The key is either the
      client_write_key or the server_write_key
requirements.condition: a client encrypts an outbound TLSCiphertext
requirements.required_behavior: use client_write_key as the AEAD key
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using server_write_key or another key
requirements.why_checkable: Role-specific key selection is visible at the AEAD call.

requirements.quote:
The key is either the
      client_write_key or the server_write_key
requirements.condition: a server encrypts an outbound TLSCiphertext
requirements.required_behavior: use server_write_key as the AEAD key
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using client_write_key or another key
requirements.why_checkable: Role-specific key selection is visible at the AEAD call.

requirements.quote:
the nonce is derived from
      the sequence number and the client_write_iv or server_write_iv
requirements.condition: a client constructs an outbound record nonce
requirements.required_behavior: derive the nonce from the record sequence number and client_write_iv
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using server_write_iv or omitting the sequence number
requirements.why_checkable: The role-specific IV and sequence-number inputs are concrete.

requirements.quote:
the nonce is derived from
      the sequence number and the client_write_iv or server_write_iv
requirements.condition: a server constructs an outbound record nonce
requirements.required_behavior: derive the nonce from the record sequence number and server_write_iv
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using client_write_iv or omitting the sequence number
requirements.why_checkable: The role-specific IV and sequence-number inputs are concrete.

requirements.quote:
the additional data input is the record header.

   I.e.,

      additional_data = TLSCiphertext.opaque_type ||
                        TLSCiphertext.legacy_record_version ||
                        TLSCiphertext.length
requirements.condition: performing AEAD encryption or decryption of TLSCiphertext
requirements.required_behavior: use opaque_type concatenated with legacy_record_version and length as additional_data
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omitting, reordering, or adding bytes to the record-header additional data
requirements.why_checkable: The authenticated additional-data byte string is defined exactly.

requirements.quote:
The plaintext input to the AEAD algorithm is the encoded
   TLSInnerPlaintext structure.
requirements.required_behavior: use the encoded TLSInnerPlaintext as the AEAD plaintext input
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using TLSPlaintext directly or excluding the inner type and padding
requirements.why_checkable: The exact plaintext byte string can be captured at the AEAD boundary.

requirements.quote:
AEADEncrypted =
          AEAD-Encrypt(write_key, nonce, additional_data, plaintext)

   The encrypted_record field of TLSCiphertext is set to AEADEncrypted.
requirements.required_behavior: set encrypted_record to AEAD-Encrypt(write_key, nonce, additional_data, plaintext)
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using different AEAD inputs or storing a value other than the AEAD output
requirements.why_checkable: The encryption function, arguments, and assigned output are exact.

requirements.quote:
plaintext of encrypted_record =
          AEAD-Decrypt(peer_write_key, nonce,
                       additional_data, AEADEncrypted)
requirements.condition: decrypting and verifying a received TLSCiphertext
requirements.required_behavior: invoke AEAD-Decrypt with peer_write_key, the record nonce, record-header additional_data, and AEADEncrypted
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using the local write key or different authenticated inputs
requirements.why_checkable: The decryption function and all four inputs are explicit.

requirements.quote:
If the decryption fails, the receiver MUST terminate the connection
   with a "bad_record_mac" alert.
requirements.required_behavior: terminate the connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: delivering plaintext or continuing record processing
requirements.why_checkable: Corrupted ciphertext has an exact terminal alert outcome.

requirements.quote:
An AEAD algorithm used in TLS 1.3 MUST NOT produce an expansion
   greater than 255 octets.
requirements.condition: selecting or using an AEAD algorithm for TLS 1.3
requirements.required_behavior: ensure its ciphertext expansion is at most 255 octets
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using an AEAD construction with expansion greater than 255 octets
requirements.why_checkable: The algorithm's maximum expansion is a fixed measurable property.
